problems.problem: BLOCKING (new, introduced by this fix) — the close-beacon cannot tell a closed window from a re-served step, so a wrong recovery phrase silently ends the run. A standalone step advances by reloading; pagehide fires, sendBeacon is fire-and-forget, and the beacon is processed AFTER the GET for the next document, not before. stillHere() at browserWizard.ts:270 fires on the GET while goneTimer is still null, then the beacon arms goneTimer at :334 and nothing ever disarms it (only a further POST does, and there is none until the user acts). 1.2s later runBrowserWizard resolves the refusal. FAILURE, driven in a real headless shell against decryptInBrowser with a real 24-word phrase: type the phrase, click 'Decrypt to a file', the CLI returns KEY_MISMATCH and re-serves the wiped step (decryptScreen.ts:237 — as does INVALID), the page comes back correctly with the CLI's reason on it — and 1194ms later the promise settles {action:'cancelled',reason:'closed'} with attempts=1. decryptCommand.ts:226 then prints 'Browser closed. Nothing was decrypted.' and returns while the person is still retyping. The socket is gone, so the retype posts into nothing: body text on the page after the CLI gave up is empty. Deterministic: 6/6 dead at pause 2500ms, 3/3 dead at 2500ms with tracing on, 3/3 alive at pause 900ms — the cliff is exactly CLOSE_GRACE_MS. Not pre-existing: the identical script at parent 02e6c99 is alive 3/3 and decrypts on the second attempt. Reachable through capy decrypt --web (the coordinator is wiring --web centrally) and through any future closeIsRefusal flow that re-serves. A fix that survives either ordering: stamp each served document with a generation counter, carry it in the beacon body, and ignore a beacon whose generation is older than the last one served — or record lastServedAt and re-check it when goneTimer fires.

MAJOR — 'a wrong phrase re-serves the step, and that reload is not mistaken for leaving' asserts exactly the right property and cannot fail on the defect. It passes only because the machine retypes 24 words and clicks inside the 1.2s grace: the whole test runs in 466ms, and the POST it sends calls stillHere() before goneTimer fires. Insert a 2s wait between `await reloaded` and the refill — the pause any human takes reading 'a single wrong word produces a completely different key' — and it fails with {action:'cancelled',reason:'closed'}. A guard that only passes when the driver is faster than a person is a false negative on the one property the beacon puts at risk.

notes: Verified independently in two throwaway detached worktrees (HEAD 7b2a1d8 and parent 02e6c99), both since removed. THE ORIGINAL BLOCKING FINDING IS GENUINELY FIXED, demonstrated not asserted: one script, run against both commits, drives a real cached chrome-headless-shell on a throwaway profile against serveSecretTable with rows carrying no `dirty` flag. At HEAD — BUTTONS ["Key","Value","Status","Updated","copy"], keyboard q/Escape/c/x post [], document holds neither sk_live nor postgres:// — closing the tab RESOLVED after 1206ms with {"action":"cancel","reason":"closed"}. At 02e6c99 the same script REJECTED after 44321ms with `CapyError: Timed out waiting for the browser (5 minutes).` Also proved in a browser at HEAD: runSecretEditorInBrowser (what editCommand.ts calls) on a clean table ends 1204ms after the tab closes, saved=null, servers=1 — it did not loop back and serve a table into a browser that had gone; serveSecretValueEditor close -> {action:'cancel',reason:'closed'}; runWebIntake close -> refusal in 1205ms with the overwrite sentence on screen and no cancel control; showDecryptResult announces its URL in 28ms (before the wait, so a caller can be the one to fetch it), the page renders '.env.main.decrypted' and '3 secrets' with no ANSI and no literal [90m, returns 376ms after load and then `fetch(url)` is refused. THE TESTS ARE REAL: I read what the three claimed blocking tests assert, not their names — 'closing a table with nothing queued ends the run as a refusal' asserts the exact settled value AND `Date.now()-t0 < 10_000` against a 30s wizard deadline, so it cannot pass by timing out; 'a run that edits nothing ends when the window closes' asserts saved===null and urls.length===1; 'closing the value editor…' asserts the settled value. All three fail without the fix (the 02e6c99 run above is the same behaviour they pin). NO SECRET LEAK: the table document holds neither plaintext, the value-editor document holds neither the plaintext nor the sk_live_51 mask fragment, the decrypt page re-serves wiped after KEY_MISMATCH with no phrase word in the document or in location.search, and the beacon body is the nonce and {} — I read closeBeaconScript and it reads nothing off the page. VERDICT IS FAIL ON ONE NEW BLOCKING REGRESSION. The mechanism chosen to give the flow an ending — a pagehide beacon believed after 1.2s unless something re-requests the document — is ordering-dependent, and the ordering goes the wrong way every time I measured it: the beacon is processed 4ms AFTER the GET it is supposed to be cancelled by. So every re-served standalone step arms a 1.2-second self-destruct, and the one flow in this parcel that re-serves is the recovery-phrase retry — the single most likely thing to happen in capy decrypt --web. That is the brief's own rule broken in a new place: the run reaches an ending the user never chose, while the page they are typing into is destroyed under them. The test written to guard exactly this property passes only because the driver is faster than a human. Everything else in the parcel is in good shape; fix the ordering (generation counter in the beacon body, or re-check lastServedAt when the grace fires), make the guard test wait out the grace, and downgrade the add --web refusal from an uncaught throw to a printed line and exit 0, and this is mergeable.
